rounds.fact: PayPal originally grew by paying users real money just to sign up and refer friends, an aggressive growth tactic that helped it become the dominant way to pay on eBay.
GameSpot launched in 1996 and became known for its numerical review scores becoming a genuine influence on game sales, sometimes controversially so.
Fark built its entire identity around submitting and voting on weird, funny news links, a simple format that predated Reddit's rise by several years.
Plenty of Fish was famously built and run by a single person for years, supported entirely by ads, before eventually being sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.
2007 was the year Netflix quietly added streaming as a bonus feature for DVD subscribers. Almost nobody noticed at the time that it would eventually replace the DVDs entirely.
